findings.description: Pre-lock plan: `sessionMark` is read after the plan's gh calls, so a change made during them is missed
`pup land`: if the audit fails after the `landed` event, overlapping sessions are never steered
findings.body:
The `landed` event is now written under the lock. So an audit that throws after it also skips the steer. It can throw on a Ctrl-C (`GateInterruptedError`) during its test run, on a `NoAdapterError`, or on a sandbox or toolchain refusal from `measureBaseline`, and `auditProject` catches none of them:

```ts
const audit = await auditProject(db, req.repoPath, req.adapters, req.gateEnv, 'keep');
steerOverlappingSessions(db, req.repoPath, session.id, mergeCommit, target, landed.targetSha);
```

Before this PR, a failed audit left no event, so re-running `pup land` landed and steered. Now the re-run refuses with "has already landed" (L71 and L152), and nothing else calls `steerOverlappingSessions`. Running sessions that overlap the landed PR are never told to take the target in (decision 99). Decision 88 hands a failed audit to `pup audit`, but it says nothing about the steer, and `pup audit` does not steer.

The steer only needs `mergeCommit`, `target` and `landed.targetSha`, all settled under the lock. Its JSDoc only requires it to run after the `landed` event. Running it before the audit restores the old guarantee. Once you move it, the test comment at `land.test.ts:632` ("The audit is the land's last step") goes stale.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/899e73785a900275bcb3ed398743e51bddf483a5/src/core/land.service.ts#L219-L223>

findings.description: On release, `dropMergeLock` renames whatever sits at the lock path aside before it checks dev/inode against the take's identity. If the held lock was removed and another run took it, this run moves that live lock aside and strands it, and a third run can then take the lock while the second is still inside. Check `directoryIdentity(lockPath)` against `identity` before the `renameSync` and leave a foreign lock in place.

`waitForLoad` runs right after the gate's own build stage. The 1-minute load average still counts the build that just exited, so the gate can wait (up to GATE_SLOT_WAIT_MS) on load it caused itself, which contradicts the comment "the load measured is the machine's and not this gate's own children". `hasSuite` is known before the build, so the wait can move above it.

`removeLockDir`'s failure message says "No run reads it; remove it from the trusted checkout", but `tryMergeLock` also calls it on the live lock path to undo a failed pid write. A pid-less lock left there blocks every later merge, so the message tells the operator a blocking leftover is harmless.

`tryMergeLock` returns `LockIdentity | number | null`, and its one caller has to tell the three cases apart with `typeof`. The taken identity is stored in a variable named `holder`. A tagged result such as `{ kind: 'taken' | 'held' | 'pidless' }` would put the contract in the type.

`waitForLoad` copies the interruptible poll loop from `acquire` in test-slot.service.ts almost line for line. `LOCK_SIGNALS` is now the third definition of the interrupt-signal set: `InterruptSignal` in sandbox.utils.ts is another, and test-slot has its own SIGINT/SIGTERM literals. That spread is how the slot wait missed SIGHUP. One exported signals constant would remove it.

The `pup merge` kept-worktree message is copied word for word from `pup land` (around L2148-2153), and `outcome.keptWorktree` is tested twice in a row. Move the kept line into the final `else`, and consider one shared print for merge and land.

The PR defines the `deadPid` helper twice, identical down to its JSDoc. `holdLock` is scoped to one describe, so the `withMergeLock` tests and land.test.ts write out `mkdirSync(lock); writeFileSync(join(lock, 'pid'), ...)` by hand. Hoist both helpers to file scope.

Three new tests repeat the same scaffold: save the real `writeFileSync`, intercept only the lock's pid path, restore it in `onTestFinished`. Only the action at the pid write differs. A file-scope `onPidWrite(pidFile, act)` helper would hold the scaffold once (`aroundPidWrite` already has this shape).

`LandRequest.wait` is always `true` in production, since `pup land` is its only caller, so the non-waiting default is reached only from tests. A future caller that forgets the flag silently refuses instead of waiting. Consider making waiting the default for land.

The new lock and load timing constants (`MERGE_LOCK_PID_FILE`, `MERGE_LOCK_POLL_MS`, `MERGE_LOCK_PID_GRACE_MS`, `RECLAIM_STALE_MS`, `LOAD_POLL_MS`, the exported `MERGE_LOCK_WAIT_MS`) live in the service file, while `MERGE_LOCK_DIRNAME` and `GATE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` sit in merge-gate.constants.ts. general.md §No hardcoded values puts them in `*.constants.ts`.
New booleans `waited`, `announced` and the `wait?: boolean` request fields don't start with is/has/should/can, as general.md §Type safety requires.

The comment "Waited for with node's default disposition..." sits above `let identity` but describes the wait loop and the `process.on` loop. Its first half repeats `withMergeLock`'s JSDoc, so keep only the same-tick point, next to the listeners. In `runMergeGate`, "The operator's and the conductor's runs wait for a live holder" repeats the `MergeRequest.wait` JSDoc (AGENTS.md §Comments).

A new module mock of `node:os`, and a wider `node:fs` mock covering `writeFileSync`, are added only to stub the load average and a pid-write failure. testing.md §When `vi.mock` is right reserves module mocks for behaviour out of scope for a test process. `waitForLoad` already takes `readLoad` and `ceiling` for injection.
One line of `reclaimMergeLock`'s JSDoc ("planted, and is replaced. Answers false when another run is reclaiming, and the caller") runs far past the wrap width of the lines around it.

In `withMergeLock`'s JSDoc, "printing one line when the wait starts, and by default not at all" reads as if the printing is what defaults to nothing. Say the default `maxWaitMs` of 0 refuses at once. The doc also doesn't mention the unannounced wait on a lock with no pid.

Decision 88's pid-less bullet says the lock is looked at again every 100 ms for a second before refusing, but that only happens in a waiting caller. With `maxWaitMs = 0` (`pup fix` and every caller other than the CLI), it refuses on the first look.

If the lock directory is gone when the locked section ends, `renameSync` in the release throws ENOENT out of the `finally` and replaces `fn`'s result. A merge that already fast-forwarded then reports a crash, and a land skips its audit and steer. The old `rmdirSync` threw the same way.
